ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals AC and BD of the rhombus ABCD intersect at point O, and $DE\parallel OC$, $CE\parallel OD$. The quadrilateral OCED is a rectangle; Given that $AC=4\sqrt{5}$ and $BD=2\sqrt{5}$, find the perimeter and area of the rectangle OCED.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \[\quad \text{Since in the rhombus } ABCD, \; OC=\frac{1}{2}AC=2\sqrt{5}, \; OD=\frac{1}{2}BD=\sqrt{5}, \\
\therefore \text{the perimeter of the rectangle } OCED \text{ is: } (2\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{5})\times 2=\boxed{6\sqrt{5}}, \text{ and the area of } OCED \text{ is: } 2\sqrt{5}\times \sqrt{5}=\boxed{10}\].
